thread:
maya: Tinybeam experiment log — spun up q3_k 13B quantized model + tiny-beam speculative policy. Initial lightweight numbers: p99 latency ~22% down, tokens/sec ~1.4x. Dropping notes for ops/eval. :eyes:

raj: Nice. Which holdout / eval harness did you use?

maya: Holdout = 10k prod-sim multi-turn prompts + 2k safety/QA holdouts. Canary A/B config: baseline = greedy on q3_k (benchserver-5), treatment = tinybeam (beam=2, early-abort threshold=0.12).

sam: Can you paste the run command?

maya: Sure — quick run we used:```bash
python run_eval.py --model rdx-13b-q3_k --policy tinybeam --beam 2 --early_abort 0.12 --holdout holdouts/prod_sim_10k.json --out results/tinybeam_run1.json
```

maya: Primary metrics: human accept-rate@top1 (crowd quickaccept), token-divergence, avg logprob-gap. Quick human pass (n=500 random) showed accept-rate delta = -0.6 percentage points (not yet statistically significant). Notable: a few hallucination-ish long-form Q&A failures popped up.

eli: Can you paste an example failure (baseline vs tinybeam) + any model logprobs? Need repro trace for SRE and safety.

maya: Example (trimmed):
```
PROMPT: "Explain CRDTs and give an example with code."
BASELINE (greedy q3_k): "CRDTs are conflict-free replicated data types... [detailed explanation + working JS pseudocode]"
TINYBEAM (beam=2, abort=0.12): "CRDTs are a type of replicated data structure... [shorter explanation, omitted convergence caveat, gave a non-compiling snippet]"
LOGPROB GAP: average token logprob (baseline)= -1.9, (tinybeam)= -2.15, divergence spikes around code block tokens.
```

raj: Looks like early-abort is truncating exploration on long, low-prob tails where you need more tokens to surface the right phrasing. Could be due to quantization jitter amplifying low-prob tails.

maya: I ran a small grid: beam=3 & abort=0.08 -> latency gains weaken (p99 down ~12%), tokens/sec ~1.2x, accept-rate delta ~-0.1pp (much closer). So tradeoff seems tunable.

perf-bot: perf-bot: summary statistics for tinybeam_run1.json -> p50 latency: 96ms -> 65ms (-32%), p99 latency: 230ms -> 180ms (-22%), tokens/sec baseline 720 -> tinybeam 960 (+1.33x).

sam: Next steps I propose:
- Full A/B sweep 100k prompts (stratified by long-answer / code / dialogue)
- Logprob traces + token-aligned diffs saved to S3 for automatic regression checks
- Run same policy across q4_x (higher-precision quant) to isolate quant noise vs policy effect
- Add localized human annotation on the 2k safety holdouts (5 reviewers each)

raj: Also add a KV-cache warmup test (cold vs warm session distribution) — speculative policies can interact badly with warm caches.

maya: Good call. I'll open a ticket and attach the little diff viewer I used (diff-tool v0.3). Will also flag the two failing prompts into the eval alert set.

sam: On it — kicking off the 100k sweep now. Command:```bash
./scripts/run_ab_sweep.sh --model rdx-13b-q3_k --policy tinybeam --beam 2 --abort 0.12 --size 100000 --out s3://redwood-eval/tinybeam/100k/
```
ETA ~8h on benchcluster (using 24 workers). :thumbsup:

maya: Awesome. If the big sweep shows accept-rate delta within -0.2pp and hallucinations are concentrated in <0.05% prompts, we can consider a 5% canary rollout with strict rollback triggers. Otherwise we'll iterate policy (beam=3/abort=0.08) or use q4_x quant for canary. :eyes: 

eli: Please paste the canary rollback criteria in the ticket (p99 latency > +10% vs baseline OR accept-rate delta < -0.5pp OR any safety holdout fail).

maya: Will do. Thanks all.

sam: Update: job started, logging to #eng-ml-eval and s3. ping me if you want interim snapshots.

raj: thanks, keeping an eye.

maya: tagging @eli and @sam for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
